front: What is Frontend Datastructure in one sentence?
back: Maps, sets, rings, and queues FE engineers use daily for UI state, caches, and render performance — not CLRS trivia.

front: Explain the mental model of Frontend Datastructure (how the system thinks).
back: Browser JS gives you Map/Set (O(1) avg keyed ops), Array (ordered, indexable), WeakMap (GC-friendly metadata). Pick structure by access pattern, not interview nostalgia.

front: Symptom: UI lag typing in big list — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: O(n) filter each keystroke · Fix: Pre-index; debounce; Progressive search functionality

front: Symptom: Memory grows unbounded — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Global cache Map · Fix: LRU cap; WeakMap for DOM-bound data

front: Symptom: Stale UI after update — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Mutated Map in place · Fix: New Map reference for React memo

front: Symptom: Wrong render order — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Object key sort · Fix: Map preserves insertion; explicit sort key

front: Symptom: Duplicate keys in virtual list — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Index as React key · Fix: Stable entity id from Map

front: Symptom: Race in async fetch — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Last-write-wins · Fix: Request id / AbortController + Map stamp

front: Gotcha with Frontend Datastructure: what silently fails?
back: Object keys are strings — obj[1] and obj["1"] collide; use Map for numeric ids.

front: When should you NOT use Frontend Datastructure?
back: < 100 items — plain array + find is fine; don't pre-optimize. Server-authoritative pagination — client Map of "all rows" fights product; page cache only. Replace DB index — client structures mirror UX needs, not SQL semantics.

front: What is Prefix sum in one sentence?
back: Precomputed cumulative totals — answer any fixed-range sum query in O(1) after O(n) preprocess; foundation for range queries, subarray counts, and difference arrays.

front: What is 2D prefix sum?
back: rectangle query in O(1).

front: What is Prefix sum + hash map?
back: count subarrays with sum k (handles negatives).

front: What is Difference array?
back: inverse of prefix sum for range updates.

front: Explain the mental model of Prefix sum (how the system thinks).
back: Build array P where P[i] = sum of arr[0..i] (0-indexed). Range sum [l, r] = P[r] - P[l-1] (define P[-1] = 0).

front: Symptom: Integer overflow — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Wrong subarray count — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: 2D query wrong — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: TLE with many queries — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: Sliding window used on negatives — what do you check and fix?

front: Gotcha with Prefix sum: what silently fails?
back: Empty subarray — count problems often need prefix 0 seeded once in the map.

front: When should you NOT use Prefix sum?
back: Non-contiguous subsequence sums — prefix sum assumes contiguous ranges. Dynamic point/range updates with interleaved queries — use Fenwick tree or segment tree. Only single full-array sum — plain loop is simpler; don't over-engineer.

front: What is Binary search in one sentence?
back: Halve sorted search space each step — O(log n) find/insert boundary; loop invariant is the hard part.

front: Explain the mental model of Binary search (how the system thinks).
back: Requires sorted array or monotonic predicate. Maintain window [left, right] where answer lies. Mid compares eliminate half. Two variants: exact match vs lower/upper bound (first position where condition holds). Off-by-one on left <= right vs left < right causes infinite loops or missed answers.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Binary search?
back: sorted: [1,3,5,7,9] target 7 → L=0 R=4 mid=2 val=5 → go right → L=3 R=4 mid=3 val=7 → found

front: Given a broken Binary search setup, what is your first validation command?
back: sorted: [1,3,5,7,9] target 7

front: Symptom: Infinite loop — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: lo/hi update · Fix: Use lo + (hi-lo)/2; ensure range shrinks

front: Symptom: Wrong index — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: <= vs < · Fix: Exact: lo<=hi; bound: half-open [lo,hi)

front: Symptom: -1 always — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Not sorted · Fix: Sort first or binary search on index space

front: Symptom: Off by one — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Post-condition · Fix: Verify lo at exit equals intended bound

front: Symptom: TLE on "sorted" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Not monotonic predicate · Fix: Prove monotonicity before binary search

front: Gotcha with Binary search: what silently fails?
back: (lo + hi) / 2 overflow — use lo + ((hi - lo) >> 1) in other languages. Duplicates — lower vs upper bound return different indices. Search on rotated array — modified invariant; don't paste vanilla template.

front: When should you NOT use Binary search?
back: Don't binary search unsorted data without transformation. Don't use when n < ~50 — linear scan simpler and cache-friendly.

front: What is Greedy algorithm in one sentence?
back: Locally optimal choice at each step — works when problem has greedy choice property and optimal substructure; otherwise wrong answer with confidence.

front: Explain the mental model of Greedy algorithm (how the system thinks).
back: At each step, pick the best-looking option now without backtracking. Fast (often O(n log n) from sorting). Proof burden is on you: exchange argument or matroid. Classic wins: interval scheduling, Huffman, Dijkstra (non-negative weights), activity selection.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Greedy algorithm?
back: Sort/preprocess → for each step pick max profit / min finish time / closest fit

front: Given a broken Greedy algorithm setup, what is your first validation command?

front: Symptom: TLE — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong sort key · Fix: Greedy usually O(n log n); avoid nested scan

front: Symptom: Suboptimal path — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Graph negative edges · Fix: Dijkstra fails — Bellman-Ford

front: Symptom: Interval bug — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Sort by wrong endpoint · Fix: Activity: sort by finish time

front: Symptom: Knapsack wrong — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Fractional vs 0/1 · Fix: Fractional greedy by value/weight; 0/1 needs DP

front: Gotcha with Greedy algorithm: what silently fails?
back: Coin change — greedy only for canonical systems; general case is NP-hard (DP). Looks right on samples — greedy failures need crafted cases in review. Stable sort matters — tie-breaking can change interval results.

front: When should you NOT use Greedy algorithm?
back: Don't greedy 0/1 knapsack or general coin change without proof. Don't skip proof in interview — state why greedy safe or pivot to DP.

front: What is Linked list in one sentence?
back: Nodes chained by next (and optionally prev) pointers — O(1) insert/delete at known node; O(n) indexed access.

front: Explain the mental model of Linked list (how the system thinks).
back: Each node holds value + next pointer. Head is entry; tail optional for O(1) append with doubly-linked + tail ref. Singly-linked: one direction. Doubly-linked: prev enables backward walk and O(1) delete given node ref. No random access — index i requires i steps from head.

Symptom: Lost rest of list — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Assignment order · Fix: node.next = node.next.next save refs first

front: Symptom: Off-by-one tail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Empty list · Fix: Dummy head; check head === null

front: Symptom: Memory leak (C/C++) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Free on delete · Fix: free(node) when removing

front: Symptom: Reverse bugs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: 3-pointer walk · Fix: prev, cur, next pattern

front: Gotcha with Linked list: what silently fails?
back: Mutating while iterating — save next before deleting current. Shared node in two lists — aliasing unless deep copy. Interview "reverse in k-group" — pointer discipline; draw diagram.

front: When should you NOT use Linked list?
back: Don't use linked list for cache-friendly bulk storage — arrays win CPU cache. Don't choose LL for frequent binary search — array + BS instead.

front: What is Sliding window in one sentence?
back: Two-pointer technique over a contiguous subarray/substring — turn O(n²) brute force into O(n) by expanding/shrinking one window instead of restarting from every index.

front: What is Fixed-size window?
back: length k given; slide L and R together.

front: What is Variable-size window?
back: maximize/minimize length subject to constraint.

front: Explain the mental model of Sliding window (how the system thinks).
back: Maintain indices left and right defining window [left, right]. Advance right to grow; advance left to shrink when a validity invariant breaks (sum too large, duplicate char seen, etc.).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Sliding window?
back: arr: [ 2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2 ] target sum ≤ 7 → L R → expand R → sum grows → if invalid → increment L until valid again → track best answer at each valid step

front: Given a broken Sliding window setup, what is your first validation command?
back: arr: [ 2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2 ] target sum ≤ 7

front: Symptom: Wrong answer on edge cases — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Empty array, all negatives, single element · Fix: Handle n === 0; pick correct algorithm (window vs prefix sum)

front: Symptom: Off-by-one length — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Inclusive [L,R] vs half-open [L,R) · Fix: Standardize: length = R - L + 1 for inclusive

front: Symptom: Infinite loop on shrink — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: left not advancing when invalid · Fix: Ensure left++ each shrink iteration

front: Symptom: TLE on large input — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Nested loops resetting left to 0 each right · Fix: left only moves forward — total O(n)

front: Symptom: Works for positives, fails with negatives — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Monotonic shrink assumption broken · Fix: Switch to prefix sum + hash map

front: Symptom: Count subarrays off by one — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Count at shrink vs expand step · Fix: Define whether each valid window counted once

front: Gotcha with Sliding window: what silently fails?
back: Non-negative numbers assumption — "minimum window with sum ≥ target" needs positive values (or non-decreasing contribution). Negative values break monotonic shrink.

front: When should you NOT use Sliding window?
back: Subsequence (non-contiguous) — window requires contiguous segment; use DP or two-pointer on sorted arrays differently. Arbitrary numeric targets with negatives — use Prefix sum + hash map. Global optimization without contiguous constraint — e.g. max subarray sum with one deletion — may need Kadane variant, not pure window.
